stem: A client has progressive dyspnea, decreased breath sounds, and dullness to percussion over one side of the chest. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
rationale: Pleural effusion can produce dyspnea, decreased breath sounds, decreased fremitus, and dullness to percussion as pleural fluid accumulates. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize physical-assessment findings associated with pleural effusion.
source_locator: History and Physical — percussion dullness, decreased breath sounds and fremitus
source_claim_supported: Pleural effusion may cause dyspnea, percussion dullness, and decreased breath sounds/fremitus over the affected area.
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — respiratory disorders and assessment findings
correction_summary: Removed irrelevant abdominal narrative, paired the key assessment findings directly with pleural effusion, and added pneumothorax as a physiologically plausible contrast. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: NCBI directly supports A. Pneumothorax generally produces hyperresonance rather than dullness; C and D do not explain the respiratory findings. Independent second pass passed.
